Hi Priya — thanks for sending this over and for the highlights. Looping in Neha (Security lead) and Kim (Privacy/Compliance) so we can produce a concise set of answers and an attached evidence doc.

Quick answers up front:
- Regional residency: our hosted API supports region-bound tenancy for commercial accounts; we have a US-only tenancy option that keeps request processing and ephemeral logs in US regions.
- Default retention: request metadata and short-term logs are retained 30 days by default. Full request/response payloads are not retained persistently unless customer enables logging or uses features that require storage (e.g., audit export).
- Deletion: account-wide erasure requests are processed within 30 days; we remove tenant-scoped logs and trigger backups retention policies (see attached for details).

We'll follow up with a short PDF with the questionnaire fields filled and a reference link to our data lifecycle playbook.

Thanks Marcus — adding a bit more precision for procurement:

1) Regional residency (hosted API):
- We offer a US-only hosted tenancy that restricts all processing and transient logs to us-east-1 and us-west-2 regional clusters. This is available on our hosted paid tiers (self-serve customers get multi-region standard).
- For contractual guarantees we include a clause that names the regions and an obligation to route and process customer requests only in those datacenters, subject to force majeure.

2) Retention specifics (defaults and optional controls):
- Default: request metadata (timestamp, token counts, model id) and system logs retained for 30 days. Error traces and alert logs retained 90 days.
- Payloads: by default we do NOT persist full request/response payloads beyond short-lived caching used for batching (seconds to minutes). Persistent logging of request content must be explicitly enabled by the customer (Audit Logging feature).
- Shorter retention: customers can request a 7-day retention profile for metadata under a managed configuration; this is subject to a short onboarding/config window.

3) Deletion & backups:
- Account-wide deletion request workflow: 1) ticket creation with support, 2) verification (2-3 business days), 3) orchestration job to scrub tenant-scoped indices and object stores (complete within 30 days), 4) post-erasure verification report.
- Backups & snapshots: we run daily snapshots; these are on a 90-day rotation. On erasure we mark tenant data for deletion on the next snapshot lifecycle pass; forensic-level unrecoverable deletion is provided for an additional compliance fee and coordination (we can provide an SLA).

4) Evidence & audit:
- We can provide an answers PDF, our data lifecycle playbook link, and a SOC 2 Type II summary that describes controls around logging and backup retention.

I attached a draft answers PDF — Marcus, Kim, please review and I’ll publish to their shared drive link.

Hi Priya — quick follow-up from Privacy:

- Third-party telemetry: we send anonymized telemetry to a small set of monitoring vendors (metrics, performance traces). We do not include customer request payloads or PII in those telemetry streams. When Audit Logging is enabled by the customer (which stores payloads to a customer-owned object bucket or our encrypted tenant store), telemetry is still scrubbed of full payload content before any external exports.

- Chain of custody: yes — for investigations we provide a time-stamped export of retained metadata and associated hashes, and that export is delivered under an auditable ticket. We can also provide signed attestations for exports as part of an evidence package (SOC report reference included).

I uploaded the finalized filled questionnaire and a one-page timeline for deletion to the shared drive: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/novolutions/compliance-answers-20280721
